component.name: View
component.summary: View and annotate PDFs, images, videos, text and 3D models
查看并标注 PDF、图片、视频、文本和 3D 模型

description.p: View is a fast, macOS Preview–style viewer for GNOME. One app opens PDFs, images, videos, spreadsheets, source code and 3D models, and lets you mark them up and sign them.

ul.li: PDFs: thumbnails, search, text selection, highlights and notes, form filling, page reordering, merging and signing
Images: markup, crop, rotate, color adjustments, export, and combining images into a PDF
Signatures drawn on the touchpad, or with a mouse, pen or finger
Live Text: select and copy text in images and scanned PDFs (optional OCR engine)
Video and audio playback with hardware decoding
CSV/TSV editor, syntax-highlighted text and code, STL/OBJ/PLY model viewer
Optional Space-bar Quick Look for GNOME Files

description.p: Combine Images into PDF in the GNOME Files right-click menu.

ul.li: Select images in Files, right-click and choose Combine Images into PDF (Convert to PDF for a single image), right in the menu instead of under Scripts. The .deb installs it automatically (it needs python3-nautilus, which it recommends); snap users enable it with a one-time command shown in the README.

description.p: Check for Updates works in the snap.

ul.li: The snap can now reach GitHub, so the update check no longer fails with a name-resolution error.

description.p: Screenshots open in View for quick markup.

ul.li: Take a screenshot (Print Screen on Linux; Snipping Tool or Win+Print Screen on Windows) and View opens it with the markup tools ready. Done (or Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+S) saves it back into the Screenshots folder and copies the edited image to the clipboard; Esc closes. On by default; turn it off in Preferences → Screenshots.
Copy Image now puts a picture on the clipboard that other apps can paste.
README in Chinese (中文).
Big photos fitted to the window are scaled down at full quality to exactly your screen's resolution instead of by the graphics card, which looked soft.
Images sit exactly on screen pixels while centred, panned or zoomed, and 100 % on a high-DPI (2x) screen repeats pixels exactly, as sharp as on a regular screen (Linux and Windows).
Images stay sharp after moving the window to a screen with different scaling.
Opening a folder shows the images in it, sorted by name.

description.p: Software updates: View checks for a new version once a day, when you open About and from Check for Updates in the menu, and installs it for you (Windows installer and .deb). Older versions stay on the Releases page.

ul.li: Windows: 3D models (STL / OBJ / PLY) work on PCs without an OpenGL driver, such as virtual machines and Remote Desktop, with built-in software rendering.
Sharper PDFs: pages are drawn on whole screen pixels, so text no longer looks soft after scrolling, zooming or moving the window between screens with different scaling (Linux and Windows).
Faster start on Windows: the first window no longer waits for the recent-files list (slow or missing network drives).
view-app --startup-trace times each startup step; About → Troubleshooting shows the same.

description.p: Snap: touchpad signing works again (View could not find the touchpad inside the sandbox even with raw-input connected), and the signature dialog now says which permission is missing.
Snap: View starts again (0.1.0 exited at launch, and the 0.1.1 snap was held in store review).

Windows: touchpad signing and touchpad drawing in Markup, the Markup toolbar button shows, videos open at once (no Direct3D decoder hang), smoother drawing, Set as Wallpaper. Text recognition on Windows.
